title: Virtual Natural History Museum for Kids
printSub: Check each hall. Doodle if you want. Page 2 cuts into hide-and-seek cards.
printHideSub: Cut the cards. Hide them. Write in the box. Ask the question.

habitats.label: Ocean Hall
habitats.challenge: Why is the ocean salty? What’s the biggest animal that ever lived?

video.title: Smithsonian Ocean Hall
video.channel: Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History

habitats.printAnswer: Salt from rocks washes into the sea and stays. The blue whale is the biggest animal we know.

habitats.label: Rainforest Hall
habitats.challenge: Why are rainforests so green? Why so many kinds of animals?
habitats.printAnswer: Lots of rain and sun grow plants in layers. More plants mean more places to eat and hide.

habitats.label: Dinosaur Hall
habitats.challenge: Why did dinosaurs get so big? Why aren’t they here now?

video.title: Dinosaur hall at the Smithsonian
video.channel: Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History

habitats.printAnswer: Some grew huge on plants or as hunters. A giant space rock and climate change ended most of them. Birds are their relatives.

habitats.label: Mammal Hall
habitats.challenge: What makes a mammal a mammal? Why fur, horns, or hooves?
habitats.printAnswer: Mammals make milk for babies and are warm-blooded. Fur keeps heat in; horns and hooves are tools and armor.
